hook: SCP-674 starts from a playful premise: an old NES Zapper that lets you shoot people on any screen, at least as far as you can see. The tone stays wry for a while, until the addendum shows what happens to someone who takes it far too seriously. The ending is a corrupted test log, so keep small technical details in mind as you go.
whyItMatters:
The effect only exists in one person's perception, which puts the question of what's real at the center of the story. It also has fun with television itself: news, cartoons and science fiction each react to a gunshot by their own rules.

That mix of comedy and paranoia makes it a quick read with a darker undertow.
thingsToNotice:
The rules matter: the change is permanent for the shooter, characters respond according to their genre, and past a certain point they start addressing the viewer directly, even warning him about the Foundation. M████ S███████ thought he was assassinating real politicians to stop a police state, watched his on-screen world slide into martial law and catastrophe instead, and died in his cell after arguing with the camera, hit by three .38 rounds while alone.

The blind spot on the right edge of the screen, mentioned early as a minor defect, comes back in the final log as a hiding place for targets who keep yelling and refuse to go down. That log was pulled from a half-melted laptop, and the doctor who wrote it is missing.
